DORA-A5.title: Governance and organisation
DORA-A5.statement: The management body defines, approves, oversees and is accountable for the implementation of the ICT risk management framework. It bears ultimate responsibility and must actively keep its knowledge up to date through regular training, proportionate to the risk managed.

requirements.DORA-A5-R1: Have the management body approve the digital operational resilience strategy and the ICT policy.
requirements.DORA-A5-R2: Assign clear roles and responsibilities for all ICT-related functions.
requirements.DORA-A5-R3: Define and approve the policy on the use of ICT third-party service providers.
requirements.DORA-A5-R4: Allocate a dedicated digital operational resilience budget and review it.
requirements.DORA-A5-R5: Have members of the management body follow regular training on ICT risk.

DORA-A5.deadline: At least annual review by the management body

DORA-A6.title: ICT risk management framework
DORA-A6.statement: Have a sound, comprehensive and documented ICT risk management framework, reviewed at least once a year, after every major incident and following audit and supervisory recommendations. An independent control function must be identified.

requirements.DORA-A6-R1: Document a framework covering ICT strategies, policies, procedures, protocols and tools.
requirements.DORA-A6-R2: Identify an independent ICT risk control function.
requirements.DORA-A6-R3: Review the framework at least annually and after every major incident.
requirements.DORA-A6-R4: Subject the framework to periodic internal audit by auditors with the required skills.
requirements.DORA-A6-R5: Set up a crisis communication plan and a process for following up audit recommendations.

DORA-A6.deadline: Annual review and after every major incident
guidance: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774: ICT risk management RTS

DORA-A7.title: ICT systems, protocols and tools
DORA-A7.statement: Use and maintain reliable ICT systems, protocols and tools, with enough capacity to absorb activity peaks, technologically resilient and sufficiently up to date. In practice, this article forbids resting a critical function on obsolete or undersized technology.

requirements.DORA-A7-R1: Use systems appropriate to the scale of operations supporting the entity's activities.
requirements.DORA-A7-R2: Size capacity to absorb peaks in orders, messages or transactions, including when new technology is deployed.
requirements.DORA-A7-R3: Ensure technological resilience to handle additional information needs under stress.
requirements.DORA-A7-R4: Keep systems up to date and free of known material failures or gaps.

evidence: Inventory of systems and their support level

DORA-A8.title: Identification of functions, assets and dependencies
DORA-A8.statement: Identify and classify business functions, the information assets and ICT assets supporting them, and all dependencies, internal and on third parties. This inventory is reviewed at least annually and at each major architecture change.

requirements.DORA-A8-R1: Identify business functions and determine which are critical or important.
requirements.DORA-A8-R2: Map the ICT assets supporting these functions and their interdependencies.
requirements.DORA-A8-R3: Identify ICT risk sources and assess relevant cyber threats.
requirements.DORA-A8-R4: Keep an inventory of existing systems and assess end-of-life systems.
requirements.DORA-A8-R5: Review these inventories at least once a year.

DORA-A8.deadline: Annual review and at each major change
evidence: Map of critical or important functions

DORA-A9.title: Protection and prevention
DORA-A9.statement: Continuously monitor and control the security and functioning of ICT systems, and deploy protection policies, procedures and tools: access management, encryption, network segmentation, change management, data leakage protection.

requirements.DORA-A9-R1: Ensure the resilience, continuity and availability of ICT systems and the security of data.
requirements.DORA-A9-R2: Implement an information security policy and least-privilege access management measures.
requirements.DORA-A9-R3: Encrypt data at rest, in transit and, where relevant, in use.
requirements.DORA-A9-R4: Segment networks and limit the attack surface.
requirements.DORA-A9-R5: Govern ICT changes with a documented validation and rollback procedure.

evidence: Access control policy and access reviews

DORA-A10.title: Detection of anomalous activities
DORA-A10.statement: Have mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities, including network performance issues and incidents, and to identify single points of failure. Multiple layers of alerts must be set up, with defined thresholds and trigger criteria.

requirements.DORA-A10-R1: Define alert thresholds and criteria triggering response processes.
requirements.DORA-A10-R2: Set up detection capabilities allowing a rapid response.
requirements.DORA-A10-R3: Dedicate sufficient resources to monitoring user activity and anomalies.
DORA-A10-R4: For trading venues, be able to detect incorrectly reported transactions.

DORA-A11.title: ICT business continuity policy
DORA-A11.statement: Put in place an ICT business continuity policy and response and recovery plans, tested at least annually. Entities other than microenterprises must have a crisis management function and report to the authorities the estimated costs and losses of major disruptions.

requirements.DORA-A11-R1: Set recovery time and recovery point objectives for each critical function.
requirements.DORA-A11-R2: Test business continuity and recovery plans at least once a year.
requirements.DORA-A11-R3: Set up a crisis management function with clear communication procedures.
requirements.DORA-A11-R4: Keep a record of activities during disruptions.
requirements.DORA-A11-R5: Estimate and report to the authorities the aggregated annual costs and losses caused by major incidents.

DORA-A12.title: Backup, restoration and redundancy
DORA-A12.statement: Define backup policies setting scope and frequency according to criticality, and restoration procedures. Backup systems must be physically and logically segregated from the source system, and restored data must be checked in an isolated environment before going back into production.

requirements.DORA-A12-R1: Define backup scope and frequency according to data criticality.
requirements.DORA-A12-R2: Physically and logically segregate backup systems from the source system.
requirements.DORA-A12-R3: Periodically test restoration procedures in an isolated environment.
requirements.DORA-A12-R4: Maintain redundant capacity with an equivalent level of resources and security.
DORA-A12-R5: For central counterparties, maintain a secondary site with a distinct geographical risk profile.

DORA-A13.title: Learning, evolving and awareness
DORA-A13.statement: Gather information on vulnerabilities and incidents, carry out post-incident reviews after every major disruption, and feed the lessons into the risk management framework. Digital resilience awareness and training programmes are mandatory for all staff and management.

requirements.DORA-A13-R1: Carry out a post-incident review after every major disruption of core activities.
requirements.DORA-A13-R2: Feed lessons learned into risk assessment and protection processes.
requirements.DORA-A13-R3: Report changes made to the competent authority on request.
requirements.DORA-A13-R4: Roll out mandatory awareness and training programmes, including for the management body.
requirements.DORA-A13-R5: Monitor relevant technological developments to anticipate their impact on ICT risk.

DORA-A13.deadline: Annual awareness, review after every major incident

DORA-A14.title: Crisis communication plans
DORA-A14.statement: Have communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of major incidents to clients, counterparts and the public, and designate at least one person in charge of communication with the public and the authorities.

requirements.DORA-A14-R1: Draw up separate communication plans for staff and for external stakeholders.
requirements.DORA-A14-R2: Designate at least one person responsible for external and institutional communication.

DORA-A16.title: Simplified framework for certain entities
DORA-A16.statement: Small and non-interconnected investment firms, exempted payment and e-money institutions and small occupational retirement institutions are exempt from Articles 5 to 15, but must still keep a lighter framework: documented ICT risk management, protection, detection, continuity, testing and third-party risk management.

requirements.DORA-A16-R1: Put in place and maintain a sound and documented ICT risk management framework.
requirements.DORA-A16-R2: Continuously monitor the security and functioning of ICT systems.
requirements.DORA-A16-R3: Reduce the impact of ICT risk through protection and prevention measures.
requirements.DORA-A16-R4: Detect anomalous activities and manage incidents.
requirements.DORA-A16-R5: Put in place continuity plans and backup, restoration and recovery measures.
requirements.DORA-A16-R6: Test these plans and measures regularly.

DORA-A17.chapter: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management and reporting
DORA-A17.title: ICT-related incident management process
DORA-A17.statement: Define and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify incidents, with early-warning indicators, identified roles and responsibilities, and escalation procedures to senior management and, where relevant, resolution authorities.

requirements.DORA-A17-R1: Set up procedures to detect, track, log and prioritise incidents.
requirements.DORA-A17-R2: Assign roles and responsibilities that can be activated for different scenarios.
requirements.DORA-A17-R3: Define communication plans towards staff, external stakeholders and the media.
requirements.DORA-A17-R4: Provide for escalation of major incidents to senior management and the management body.

DORA-A18.chapter: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management and reporting
DORA-A18.title: Classification of incidents and cyber threats
DORA-A18.statement: Classify incidents against seven criteria: number of clients or counterparts affected, reputation, duration and service downtime, geographical spread, data losses, criticality of the services affected, economic impact. Materiality thresholds are set by Delegated Regulation 2024/1772.

requirements.DORA-A18-R1: Apply the seven classification criteria to each incident.
requirements.DORA-A18-R2: Determine whether it is major against the materiality thresholds of the technical standards.
requirements.DORA-A18-R3: Also classify significant cyber threats according to their criticality.

DORA-A19.chapter: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management and reporting
DORA-A19.title: Reporting major incidents to the competent authority
DORA-A19.statement: Report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority according to three deadlines set by Delegated Regulation 2025/301: initial notification, intermediate report, final report. Reporting uses mandatory harmonised templates.

requirements.DORA-A19-R1: Send the initial notification within the deadlines set by the technical standards.
requirements.DORA-A19-R2: Send an intermediate report once the situation is restored, then at each significant change.
requirements.DORA-A19-R3: Send a final report including root-cause analysis.
requirements.DORA-A19-R4: Use the Article 20 harmonised templates; report any technical impossibility by other means.
requirements.DORA-A19-R5: Inform affected clients when the incident has an impact on their financial interests.

DORA-A19.deadline: Initial notification, intermediate report, final report
evidence: Timestamped reports to the ACPR or AMF
guidance: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301: content and deadlines for reporting

DORA-A24.chapter: Chapter IV: Digital operational resilience testing
DORA-A24.title: Digital operational resilience testing programme
DORA-A24.statement: Set up a sound and comprehensive testing programme, proportionate to size and risk profile, as an integral part of the ICT risk management framework. Tests are carried out by independent parties, internal or external, and all deficiencies found must be remediated on an agreed schedule.

requirements.DORA-A24-R1: Define a testing programme covering all ICT systems supporting critical or important functions.
requirements.DORA-A24-R2: Ensure testers are independent and prevent conflicts of interest.
requirements.DORA-A24-R3: Set up procedures to prioritise, classify and remediate deficiencies found.
requirements.DORA-A24-R4: Test systems supporting critical or important functions at least once a year.

DORA-A24.deadline: Annual tests on critical or important functions

DORA-A25.chapter: Chapter IV: Digital operational resilience testing
DORA-A25.title: Range of tests required
DORA-A25.statement: Carry out an appropriate range of tests: vulnerability assessments, open-source analyses, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, questionnaires and scanning software, source code reviews, compatibility, performance, end-to-end and penetration tests.

requirements.DORA-A25-R1: Carry out vulnerability assessments and network security analyses.
requirements.DORA-A25-R2: Carry out source code reviews where feasible.
requirements.DORA-A25-R3: Carry out performance, end-to-end and penetration tests.
requirements.DORA-A25-R4: Test continuity and recovery plans as part of the programme.

DORA-A25.deadline: According to the testing programme, at least annually

DORA-A26.chapter: Chapter IV: Digital operational resilience testing
DORA-A26.title: Threat-led penetration testing
DORA-A26.statement: Financial entities identified by the authorities carry out threat-led penetration testing at least every three years, on live production systems supporting critical or important functions. The methodology is aligned with TIBER-EU and the scope is validated by the competent authority, which then issues an attestation.
appliesTo: Financial entities identified by the competent authority

requirements.DORA-A26-R1: Identify the systems, processes and technologies supporting critical or important functions, including outsourced ones.
requirements.DORA-A26-R2: Have the test scope validated by the competent authority.
requirements.DORA-A26-R3: Involve the relevant ICT third-party service providers in the test.
requirements.DORA-A26-R4: Implement risk management controls to test in production without compromising services.
requirements.DORA-A26-R5: Obtain the authority's attestation confirming the test's compliance.

DORA-A28.chapter: Chapter V: Managing ICT third-party risk
DORA-A28.title: General principles of ICT third-party risk management
DORA-A28.statement: Manage ICT third-party risk as an integral part of ICT risk, under the full responsibility of the financial entity. Adopt a third-party risk strategy, keep a register of information on all contractual arrangements, and submit it annually to the competent authority.

requirements.DORA-A28-R1: Adopt an ICT third-party risk strategy approved by the management body.
requirements.DORA-A28-R2: Keep a register of information in line with the templates of Implementing Regulation 2024/2956.
requirements.DORA-A28-R3: Distinguish in the register the arrangements supporting critical or important functions.
requirements.DORA-A28-R4: Submit the register to the competent authority at least once a year and on request.
requirements.DORA-A28-R5: Inform the authority in good time of any planned arrangement covering critical or important functions.
requirements.DORA-A28-R6: Report annually to the authority the number of new arrangements concluded.

DORA-A28.deadline: Register submitted annually to the competent authority
evidence: Register of information in the fifteen templates
guidance: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956: register of information templates

DORA-A29.chapter: Chapter V: Managing ICT third-party risk
DORA-A29.title: Preliminary assessment of concentration risk
DORA-A29.statement: Before entering an arrangement covering a critical or important function, assess concentration risk: reliance on a provider that is hard to substitute, reliance on several closely connected providers, and the consequences of a failure. Examine subcontracting chains and their impact on oversight capability.

requirements.DORA-A29-R1: Assess, before contracting, the concentration risk linked to the intended provider.
requirements.DORA-A29-R2: Analyse the provider's substitutability and the conditions for effective reversibility.
requirements.DORA-A29-R3: Examine subcontracting chains, in particular towards third countries.
requirements.DORA-A29-R4: Weigh the benefits and costs of alternative solutions.

guidance: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/532: subcontracting of critical ICT services

DORA-A30.chapter: Chapter V: Managing ICT third-party risk
DORA-A30.title: Mandatory contractual provisions
DORA-A30.statement: Include in each ICT contract the minimum terms of Article 30(2) and, for critical or important functions, the reinforced terms of paragraph 3: quantitative service levels, cooperation in penetration tests, unrestricted access and audit rights, exit strategies and transition periods.

requirements.DORA-A30-R1: Describe precisely the ICT functions and services, the location of data and processing, and notification of any change.
requirements.DORA-A30-R2: Provide for data availability, integrity and confidentiality requirements.
requirements.DORA-A30-R3: Guarantee assistance during incidents, participation in training, and unrestricted access and audit.
requirements.DORA-A30-R4: Set quantitative and qualitative performance targets for critical or important functions.
requirements.DORA-A30-R5: Govern further subcontracting and the conditions for changing it.
requirements.DORA-A30-R6: Provide for exit strategies with sufficient transition periods.
requirements.DORA-A30-R7: Define termination rights and notice periods.

DORA-A30.deadline: Applies to every ICT arrangement in force

DORA-A31.title: Oversight of critical third-party providers
DORA-A31.statement: Third-party providers designated as critical by the European supervisory authorities are subject to direct EU oversight, led by a lead overseer supported by joint examination teams. For the client financial entity, the consequence is twofold: it must take into account recommendations addressed to the provider, and stop using a service when the overseer requires it.

requirements.DORA-A31-R1: Identify among its providers those on the list of designated critical third-party providers.
requirements.DORA-A31-R2: Take the lead overseer's recommendations into account in third-party risk management.
requirements.DORA-A31-R3: Be able to suspend or terminate the use of a service when the overseer requires it.
DORA-A31-R4: For a designated provider: maintain an adequate presence in the Union within twelve months of designation.

evidence: Records of how recommendations were taken into account

DORA-A45.title: Sharing cyber threat information
DORA-A45.statement: Financial entities may exchange cyber threat information and intelligence among themselves, within trusted communities, under conditions that protect the commercially sensitive nature of the information and respect data protection law.

requirements.DORA-A45-R1: Use sharing arrangements that protect the confidentiality of the information exchanged.
requirements.DORA-A45-R2: Notify the competent authority of participation in such an arrangement.
